full_page.content:
1947, March 5
Mrs. Maxine Cavanaugh
Page 2.
Most probably the trouble of which you complain is an effect, a simple consequence of want of this science, lack of religion. Che is almost forced to conclude that neither of you are much advanced in this appallingly neglected science. .. As to what your husband was once upon a time is a mighty small matter for him to "bank on". He certainly was never one of the Apostals or an archangel. .... Judas was. Lucifer was. If he has given up the exercise of faith in God and the fostering of religion, rather I'll say that inasmuch as any of us fail in this vital matter, in just so much does the individual stand in danger falling a prey of Hell.
Some ten years ago there was a fearfully tragic death in Detroit. A ce tain judge who as a young man had elicited high compliments publicly given as a "practical model of a young Catholic". Even in his youth, however, it would seem the same judge had been naturally inclined to petty jealousy. Whatever the cause, he had little by little given up the practice of his faith - the sad way we are all inclined - and finally abandoned religion entirely and in the end went and hanged himself. Kay the dear Lord preserve us such a fate!
(unfinished)
